A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HJ-Prox operator-splitting work. Their main text, equations, five figures, references, and Appendices A–H are readable and support a complete comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original optimization experiments on simulated regression, signal and image reconstruction, and GSE2034 gene-expression data, with results in Figures 1–5.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results and adds qualitative observations about sensitivity to the smoothing schedule in Appendix H.

M1.justification: The HJ-Prox estimator, splitting updates in Equations (8)–(12), and hybrid use of exact and approximate proximals remain unchanged. Revised convergence conditions do not introduce a different algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions cover the same seven problems: LASSO, sparse group LASSO, total variation, trend filtering, multitask learning, non-negative LASSO, and overlapping group LASSO on GSE2034. Appendix H.7's preprocessing corrections do not introduce different task or dataset coverage.

E2.justification: Figures 1–5 retain the same comparators within corresponding experiments, including analytical PGD/DRS/DYS/PDHG, HJ-PPM, the DYS-HJ variants, and FoGLASSO. Newly cited works are not added experimental baselines.

E3.justification: Appendix H.7 removes the statement that a two-sample t-test retains the top 1,000 genes and changes Equation (175) from 289 to 298 groups. This reconciles the reported setup with the retained 13,237-feature dimensions and Section 4.4's 298 groups. These are reported protocol corrections; the PDFs do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: Appendix H adds a brief qualitative sensitivity report: convergence tolerates departures from the prescribed smoothing decay, and schedules between approximately 1/k and 1/k² produce the best solution quality. No detailed sweep or supporting plot is added; existing splitting and hybrid comparisons are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, error bars, or performance significance tests. The new discussion of alpha_k explains an existing theoretical probability bound. The removed t-test statement concerns feature preprocessing rather than uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Numerical results in Figures 1–5 are unchanged, including Figure 5's objectives of 38.345 for FoGLASSO and 38.363 for DYS-HJ. Appendix H newly reports the qualitative finding that smoothing schedules between approximately 1/k and 1/k² give the best solution quality.

T1.justification: Theorems 3.5, 3.6, 3.8, and 3.9, together with their appendix restatements, add L-Lipschitz assumptions, substantially narrowing the stated domain of the central convergence guarantees. PGD's admissible step-size bound also changes from 2/L to 1/L′, with L′ denoting smoothness. The principal error bounds and proof arguments otherwise remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same main claims: a unified HJ-Prox splitting framework, almost-sure convergence under regularity conditions, and competitive empirical solutions. The formal restrictions are revised in the theorem statements.

C2.justification: Appendix H newly explains that alpha_k is a proof device rather than an algorithmic hyperparameter and that faster decay inflates the theoretically sufficient sample budget. It recommends slower summable schedules. Existing discussions of approximation tradeoffs and the theory–practice gap remain.

D1.justification: v3 replaces the promise of code upon publication with a specific GitHub repository and newly specifies p = 0.00001 for the smoothing schedule. Appendix H.7 also corrects preprocessing documentation. The PDFs do not establish that the newly disclosed exponent represents a changed implementation.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations to Zhang et al. (2025) on hybrid SAT solving and McKenzie et al. (2024) on differentiating integer programs. It also supplies a Bach (2013) reference for a previously broken citation. The central positioning relative to prior proximal and splitting methods remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Localized edits correct grammar, punctuation, capitalization, and a malformed citation; Appendix H gains explanatory prose, and an Impact Statement is added. The main narrative and ordering of Sections 1–6 and Appendices A–H remain intact.

P2.justification: All five figures, their captions, and the group-norm table within Figure 5 retain their presentation. The proceedings footer, added Impact Statement, and expanded text produce limited column and page-layout reflow in the introduction, references, and appendices.

improvement.justification: v3 makes previously omitted Lipschitz restrictions explicit and tightens PGD's step-size condition to match Lemma D.1. It also resolves conflicting gene/group descriptions and provides concrete code-access information and a smoothing exponent. These improve precision and reproducibility. The gains remain limited: most proofs and all plotted results are unchanged, and the new schedule-robustness assertion lacks a documented supporting sweep.
